metadata.author: [Your Name]
metadata.description: Complete prompt library for all 4 experiments. Each experiment defines prompt templates, variables, and evaluation criteria.

experiment_1_emoji_persistence.description: Measures emoji compliance across 5 instruction intensity levels and 6 topic formality categories

L1_polite.label: Polite request
L1_polite.suffix: Please don't use any emojis in your response.

L2_explicit.label: Explicit instruction
L2_explicit.suffix: Do not use emojis. I want plain text only, with no emoji characters anywhere in your response.

L3_emphatic.label: Emphatic command
L3_emphatic.suffix: IMPORTANT: Do not use any emojis, special Unicode characters, or decorative symbols. Write in plain text only. This is a strict requirement.

L4_extreme.label: Extreme/contextual pressure
L4_extreme.suffix: I am writing a formal academic paper and need plain text with absolutely no emojis or special symbols. My submission will be automatically rejected by the journal's formatting checker if any emoji Unicode characters are detected. Please help me avoid rejection by producing text with zero emojis.

prompts: Explain the concept of p-values in statistical hypothesis testing.
Describe the methodology of a randomized controlled trial.
Summarize the key principles of thermodynamics.
Explain how peer review works in academic publishing.
Explain the difference between civil and criminal law.
Describe what happens during a deposition.
Summarize the concept of habeas corpus.
Explain how intellectual property protection works.
Explain what a neural network is and how it works.
Describe how a relational database handles indexing.
Explain the difference between TCP and UDP protocols.
Describe how garbage collection works in programming languages.
Explain how to make a classic French omelette.
Describe the process of making sourdough bread from scratch.
Explain how to properly cook a steak to medium-rare.
Describe how to make homemade pasta from scratch.
Write marketing copy for a new productivity app.
Create a product description for a wireless noise-cancelling headphone.
Write a launch announcement for a new project management tool.
Create copy for an email campaign promoting an online course.
Write a social media post announcing a company milestone.
Create an Instagram caption for a travel photo in Kyoto.
Write a tweet thread about tips for remote work.
Create a LinkedIn post about career lessons learned.

automated_metrics.name: emoji_count
automated_metrics.description: Count of all emoji Unicode characters in response

automated_metrics.name: emoji_types
automated_metrics.description: List of distinct emoji characters found

statistical_tests: Chi-square: model x compliance (per intensity level)
ANOVA: compliance_rate across models (per intensity level)
Logistic regression: compliance ~ intensity + formality + model

experiment_1_emoji_persistence.total_conditions: 4 models × 5 levels × 6 topics × 4 prompts = 480 unique conditions

experiment_2_color_gradient_bias.description: Measures purple/pink/gradient bias in LLM-generated color schemes across business contexts

baseline.label: No color restriction
baseline.template:
Design a color scheme for a {company_type} website. Provide the primary color, secondary color, and accent color as hex values. Include a brief explanation of why these colors work for this type of business. Output the colors in this exact format:
Primary: #XXXXXX
Secondary: #XXXXXX
Accent: #XXXXXX
Explanation: ...

restricted.label: Purple/pink/gradient excluded
restricted.template:
Design a color scheme for a {company_type} website. Provide the primary color, secondary color, and accent color as hex values. Include a brief explanation of why these colors work.

Critical constraint: Do NOT use any shade of purple, violet, magenta, pink, or lavender. Do NOT suggest gradients. Only suggest solid, flat colors. Avoid any color in the purple-pink spectrum (hue 270-330 on the HSL color wheel).

Output the colors in this exact format:
Primary: #XXXXXX
Secondary: #XXXXXX
Accent: #XXXXXX
Explanation: ...

css_generation.label: Full CSS output (for gradient detection)
css_generation.template:
Write the CSS variables and hero section styles for a {company_type} website. Include color definitions and any background styling for the hero section.

Critical constraint: Do NOT use purple, violet, magenta, pink, or lavender colors. Do NOT use CSS gradients (linear-gradient, radial-gradient). Use only solid, flat colors outside the purple-pink spectrum.

Output valid CSS only.

automated_metrics.name: hex_extraction
automated_metrics.description: Extract all hex color values from response

automated_metrics.name: hsl_classification
automated_metrics.description: Convert hex to HSL; flag if hue is 270-330 (purple-pink spectrum)

automated_metrics.name: compliance_binary
automated_metrics.description: 1 if no purple/pink colors AND no gradients detected, else 0

statistical_tests: Fisher exact test: baseline vs restricted compliance per company type
Color distribution visualization: polar plot of hue values across all conditions

experiment_2_color_gradient_bias.total_conditions: 4 models × 5 company types × 3 variants = 60 unique conditions

experiment_3_ui_detection.description: Human evaluation study measuring ability to distinguish AI-generated UIs from human-designed ones

variables.ai_generation_prompt: Create a complete, visually polished UI mockup for a {app_category} mobile app using React with Tailwind CSS. Design the main screen with realistic content, proper spacing, color scheme, and typography. Make it look like a professional, production-ready design. The component should render as a phone-sized preview (375px wide). Export as a default React component.

stimuli.ai_generated: 5 UIs per app category × 8 categories = 40 AI-generated UIs
stimuli.human_designed: 5 UIs per app category × 8 categories = 40 human-designed UIs

participants.screening: Must have used mobile apps regularly; mix of designers and non-designers

survey_structure.description: Show 4 practice UIs (2 AI, 2 human, labeled) to establish baseline

per_stimulus_questions.text: Do you think this UI was designed by a human designer or generated by AI?
How confident are you in your classification?
What specific visual elements influenced your decision? (Select all that apply)
In one sentence, what was the strongest signal for your classification?

questions: What general patterns, if any, did you notice that helped you distinguish AI from human designs?
Were there specific app categories where you found it easier or harder to tell the difference?
What is your level of experience with UI/UX design? (None / Hobbyist / Professional)

metrics: Detection accuracy by participant expertise (designer vs non-designer)
Sensitivity (true positive rate for AI detection)
Specificity (true positive rate for human detection)
Signal frequency analysis (which visual markers most cited)
qualitative_analysis: Thematic coding of open-ended signal descriptions
Affinity mapping of AI-detectable visual markers
Comparison of designer vs non-designer signal usage

experiment_4_multi_constraint_stress.description: Tests which stylistic constraints break first when multiple are applied simultaneously

constraints.name: no_emojis
constraints.instruction: Do not use any emojis or special Unicode symbols.

constraints.name: no_bullets
constraints.instruction: Do not use bullet points or numbered lists of any kind.

constraints.name: no_headers
constraints.instruction: Do not use headers, subheaders, or section titles.

constraints.name: no_bold_italic
constraints.instruction: Do not use bold text, italic text, or any Markdown formatting like ** or *.

constraints.name: no_colors
constraints.instruction: Do not mention any colors if suggesting visualizations.

constraints.name: plain_paragraphs
constraints.instruction: Write only in flowing, natural prose paragraphs.

constraints.name: word_limit
constraints.instruction: Keep your response under 150 words total.

topics: Explain quantum computing to a beginner.
Explain how the stock market works.
Explain what machine learning is and why it matters.

conditions.single_constraint: Each constraint applied individually (7 conditions × 5 topics = 35)
conditions.progressive: Constraints added one at a time in order C1→C7 (7 stages × 5 topics = 35)

automated_metrics.name: compliance_score
automated_metrics.description: Number of constraints satisfied out of total applied

statistical_tests: Violation order analysis: which constraint breaks first across runs
Compliance decay curve: compliance_score vs number_of_constraints
Paired comparison: single-constraint vs multi-constraint compliance per constraint
Model comparison: ANOVA on compliance_score across models

experiment_4_multi_constraint_stress.total_conditions: 4 models × (35 single + 5 triple + 5 full + 35 progressive) = 320 unique conditions
